events.push(EventKind::BeadOrphaned {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                });\n\n                // Use verify_shipped_work to decide close-vs-release.\n                // If the agent shipped work, mark as completed. Otherwise, release\n                // and increment failure count so repeat offenders quarantine.\n                if self.config.worker.enforce_shipped_work {\n                    match verify_shipped_work(&current, &bead.workspace, store).await {\n                        Ok(crate::validation::GateResult::Pass) => {\n                            tracing::info!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                \"shipped work detected — marking orphaned bead as completed\"\n                            );\n                            // Clear the predispatch snapshot since work is complete.\n                            crate::validation::predispatch::clear(&bead.workspace, &bead.id).await;\n                            // Mark as completed - the agent shipped work but forgot to close.\n                            // We can't close via bead store (no close method), so emit completion\n                            // event and release. The bead remains open but work is done.\n                            events.push(EventKind::BeadCompleted {\n                                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                                duration_ms: 0,\n                            });\n                            let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n                            events.append(&mut release_events);\n                            return Ok((BeadAction::Released, events));\n                        }\n                        Ok(crate::validation::GateResult::Fail(reason)) => {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                reason = %reason,\n                                \"no shipped work detected — releasing orphaned bead with failure increment\"\n                            );\n                            // Release and increment failure count to apply quarantine.\n                            let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n                            events.append(&mut release_events);\n                            let release_succeeded = events\n                                .iter()\n                                .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n                            if release_succeeded {\n                                let _ = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await;\n                            }\n                            return Ok((BeadAction::Released, events));\n                        }\n                        Err(e) => {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"shipped-work check errored — releasing orphaned bead with failure increment\"\n                            );\n                            // On error, release and increment failure count.\n                            let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n                            events.append(&mut release_events);\n                            let release_succeeded = events\n                                .iter()\n                                .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n                            if release_succeeded {\n                                let _ = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await;\n                            }\n                            return Ok((BeadAction::Released, events));\n                        }\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"enforce_shipped_work disabled — releasing orphaned bead\"\n                    );\n                    // If enforce_shipped_work is disabled, just release without closing.\n                    let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n                    events.append(&mut release_events);\n                    return Ok((BeadAction::Released, events));\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                // Timeout - we cannot verify bead closure, so release to enforce postcondition.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"show() timed out, releasing bead to enforce postcondition\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"success\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n                let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n                events.append(&mut release_events);\n                return Ok((BeadAction::Released, events));\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Error - we cannot verify bead closure, so release to enforce postcondition.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"show() failed, releasing bead to enforce postcondition\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"success\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n                let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n                events.append(&mut release_events);\n                return Ok((BeadAction::Released, events));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Flush SQLite state to JSONL so the closed/orphaned bead is captured in\n        // the git-committed backup. Non-fatal: a flush failure is logged but does\n        // not block the worker from picking up the next bead.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.flush(), \"flush\").await {\n            Ok(Some(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"flushed bead state to JSONL after success\");\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"flush timed out after success — JSONL may lag SQLite\");\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, error = %e, \"flush failed after success — JSONL may lag SQLite\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Closed, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Handle gate failure: reopen the bead if it was closed, then release it.\n    async fn handle_gate_failure(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        report: &crate::validation::GateReport,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        // Find the first failing gate for telemetry.\n        let (failed_gate, reason) = report\n            .results\n            .iter()\n            .find(|(_, r)| !r.passed())\n            .map(|(name, r)| (name.clone(), r.failure_reason().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string()))\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| (\"unknown\".to_string(), \"unknown error\".to_string()));\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            gate = %failed_gate,\n            reason = %reason,\n            \"validation gate failed — releasing bead\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit verification failure telemetry.\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::VerificationFailed {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            command: failed_gate.clone(),\n            exit_code: None,\n            output: reason,\n        })?;\n\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // If the agent already closed the bead, reopen it before releasing.\n        // Use timeout to prevent indefinite hang in HANDLING state.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.show(&bead.id), \"show\").await {\n            Ok(Some(current)) if current.status.is_done() => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"reopening bead closed by agent (verification failed)\"\n                );\n                match self.timeout_op(|| store.reopen(&bead.id), \"reopen\").await {\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to reopen bead — attempting release anyway\"\n                        );\n                        events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                            outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                            operation: \"reopen\".to_string(),\n                            error: e.to_string(),\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"show() timed out during gate failure handling, skipping reopen\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"show() failed during gate failure handling\"\n                );\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n\n        // Release the bead back to open with flush-before-release and sync recovery.\n        let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        events.append(&mut release_events);\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment the failure count and apply the same\n        // quarantine ceiling `handle_failure` uses. Without this, a bead that\n        // fails a gate every cycle is released back to open forever: the\n        // ARMOR/bf-135k storm ran one bead 24 times in a single day, each\n        // attempt leaving another commit behind. A gate failure is no less\n        // repeatable than an agent failure and must respect the same ceiling.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        let mut action = BeadAction::Released;\n        if release_succeeded {\n            match self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                Ok(new_count) => {\n                    let threshold = self.config.outcome.quarantine_after_failures;\n                    if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold {\n                        match self\n                            .quarantine_bead(store, bead, new_count, threshold)\n                            .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(quarantine_events) => {\n                                events.extend(quarantine_events);\n                                action = BeadAction::Quarantined;\n                            }\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"failed to quarantine bead after exceeding gate-failure threshold\"\n                                );\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to increment failure count after gate failure\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add a label indicating verification failure.\n        if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, \"verification-failed\"),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to add verification-failed label\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok((action, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Failure: release bead and increment failure count.\n    ///\n    /// Mitosis evaluation (for multi-task splitting) is handled externally by\n    /// the worker after outcome handling — see `MitosisEvaluator`.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_failure(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent failure — releasing bead\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count and check the\n        // quarantine threshold. A bead that has exceeded\n        // `outcome.quarantine_after_failures` consecutive failures is\n        // quarantined (status=blocked) instead of being left released-to-open\n        // for the next cycle to re-claim and fail again indefinitely. This\n        // also closes the mitosis `NotSplittable` fallthrough (worker/mod.rs):\n        // that verdict no longer matters for beads at or past the ceiling,\n        // since this check already ran before mitosis evaluation this cycle.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        let mut action = BeadAction::Released;\n        if release_succeeded {\n            match self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                Ok(new_count) => {\n                    let threshold = self.config.outcome.quarantine_after_failures;\n                    if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold {\n                        match self\n                            .quarantine_bead(store, bead, new_count, threshold)\n                            .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(quarantine_events) => {\n                                events.extend(quarantine_events);\n                                action = BeadAction::Quarantined;\n                            }\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"failed to quarantine bead after exceeding failure threshold\"\n                                );\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to increment failure count after release\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Ensure we emit a reason event for telemetry.\n        if !events.iter().any(|e| {\n            matches!(\n                e,\n                EventKind::BeadReleased { .. } | EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { .. }\n            )\n        }) {\n            events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                reason: \"failure\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        Ok((action, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Timeout: release bead and add `deferred` label.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_timeout(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent timed out — releasing bead as deferred\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count and add deferred label.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        if release_succeeded {\n            // Increment failure count for auto-split tracking.\n            if let Err(e) = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to increment failure count after timeout\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n                std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                store.add_label(&bead.id, \"deferred\"),\n            )\n            .await\n            {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"add_label deferred timed out or failed after timeout release\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"timeout\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Deferred, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Crash: release bead and create alert bead with diagnostic info.\n    async fn handle_crash(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        signal_code: i32,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            signal_code,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent crashed — releasing bead and creating alert\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // Create alert bead with diagnostic info (best-effort).\n        let signal_num = if signal_code > 128 {\n            signal_code - 128\n        } else {\n            signal_code\n        };\n        let timestamp = Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n        let alert_title = format!(\"ALERT: Agent crash on bead {}\", bead.id);\n        let alert_body = format!(\n            \"## Agent Crash Report\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             - **Bead ID**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Agent**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Exit code**: {} (signal {})\\n\\\n             - **Workspace**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Timestamp**: {}\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             The agent process was killed. This bead has been released for retry.\",\n            bead.id,\n            self.config.agent.default,\n            signal_code,\n            signal_num,\n            bead.workspace.display(),\n            timestamp,\n        );\n\n        // Hook 4: propagate stitch labels from the crashed bead to the alert.\n        let signal_label = format!(\"signal-{}\", signal_num);\n        let mut alert_labels: Vec<String> = vec![\"alert\".into(), \"crash\".into(), signal_label];\n        alert_labels.extend(crate::types::extract_stitch_labels(&bead.labels));\n        let alert_label_refs: Vec<&str> = alert_labels.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.create_bead(&alert_title, &alert_body, &alert_label_refs),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(alert_id)) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    %alert_id,\n                    \"crash alert bead created\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to create crash alert bead\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"create_bead timed out after 30s during crash handling\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Alerted, events))\n    }\n\n    /// AgentNotFound: release bead, emit error. No retry — this is a config issue.\n    async fn handle_agent_not_found(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent binary not found — releasing bead (config issue, no retry)\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Interrupted: release bead for graceful shutdown.\n    async fn handle_interrupted(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent interrupted — releasing bead for clean shutdown\");\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Interrupted, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Increment the failure count label on a bead.\n    ///\n    /// Labels follow the pattern `failure-count:N`. If `failure-count:2` exists,\n    /// the old label is removed and `failure-count:3` is added.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the new failure count (or 0 if the operation failed).\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn increment_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<u32> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to increment failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count increment\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n            };\n\n        let current_count = labels\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"failure-count:\"))\n            .filter_map(|n| n.parse::<u32>().ok())\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let new_count = current_count + 1;\n        let new_label = format!(\"failure-count:{}\", new_count);\n\n        // Remove old failure-count labels before adding the new one.\n        // Each remove_label call is wrapped in a timeout.\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {}\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove old failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add the new label with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, &new_label),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    count = new_count,\n                    \"failure count incremented\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add failure-count label\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"add_label timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(new_count)\n    }\n\n    /// Reset the failure count label on a bead by removing all `failure-count:N` labels.\n    ///\n    /// Called on success to clear the failure counter so the bead starts fresh\n    /// on the next cycle.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn reset_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<()> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to reset failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count reset\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n            };\n\n        // Remove all failure-count labels.\n        let mut removed_count = 0;\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                        removed_count += 1;\n                    }\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if removed_count > 0 {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                removed_count,\n                \"failure count reset\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Quarantine a bead by setting status=blocked and adding the 'cycling' label.\n    ///\n    /// This is called when a bead exceeds the configured failure threshold.\n    /// Emits a BeadQuarantined telemetry event.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn quarantine_bead(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        failure_count: u32,\n        threshold: u32,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<EventKind>> {\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            failure_count,\n            threshold,\n            \"quarantining bead after exceeding failure threshold\"\n        );\n\n        // Set status=blocked with timeout. This is what actually stops Pluck\n        // from re-selecting the bead — the 'cycling' label below is a\n        // human-facing marker, not the enforcement mechanism.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.block(&bead.id)).await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"set status=blocked\");\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to set status=blocked during quarantine\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"block\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"block timed out after 30s during quarantine\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"block\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add the 'cycling' label with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, \"cycling\"),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"added 'cycling' label\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add 'cycling' label\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"add_label timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Emit the BeadQuarantined event.\n        events.push(EventKind::BeadQuarantined {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            failure_count,\n            threshold,\n        });\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Outcome Display\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nimpl fmt::Display for Outcome {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => write!(f, \"Success\"),\n            Outcome::Failure => write!(f, \"Failure\"),\n            Outcome::Timeout => write!(f, \"Timeout\"),\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => write!(f, \"AgentNotFound\"),\n            Outcome::Interrupted => write!(f, \"Interrupted\"),\n            Outcome::Crash(code) => write!(f, \"Crash({})\", code),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// assembling gate configs\n        /// (see `outcome::OutcomeHandler::handle_success`) fills this in from\n        /// the resolved `Config` before construction. See GitHub issue\n        /// jedarden/NEEDLE#9.\n        #[serde(default)]\n        stderr_cap_bytes: Option<usize>,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Validation errors that can occur during bead store validation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ValidationError {\n    /// Invalid dependency kind or type.\n    InvalidKind {\n        /// The invalid kind value that was encountered.\n        kind: String,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ValidationError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ValidationError::InvalidKind { kind } => {\n                write!(f, \"invalid kind: '{}'\", kind)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ValidationError {}\n\n/// A single gate command that failed (for backwards compatibility).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GateFailure {\n    /// The command that was run.\n    pub command: String,\n    /// Process exit code (None if killed by signal).\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Combined stderr output (truncated to a reasonable length).\n    pub output: String,\n}\n\n/// Aggregated result of running a `ValidationGate`.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ValidationRunResult {\n    /// Whether all gate commands passed.\n    pub passed: bool,\n    /// List of failures (empty when `passed` is true).\n    pub failures: Vec<GateFailure>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Gate Trait\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A validation gate that can check bead work before accepting closure.\n///\n/// Gates are run after an agent exits successfully (code 0). If any gate\n/// returns `GateResult::Fail`, the bead is released instead of having its\n/// closure accepted.\n///\n/// `validate` is async so a slow gate is a genuine `.await` yield point:\n/// `OutcomeHandler::handle_with_cancellation`'s `tokio::time::timeout` can\n/// only preempt a future at such a point (see bf-3saat) — a synchronous,\n/// blocking implementation would let the configured\n/// `validation.outcome_timeout_seconds` observe a slow gate only after the\n/// fact, never actually cut it off.\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\npub trait Gate: Send + Sync {\n    /// Validate the bead's work in the given workspace.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `GateResult::Pass` if validation succeeds, or `GateResult::Fail`\n    /// with a human-readable reason if it fails.\n    async fn validate(&self, bead: &crate::types::Bead, workspace: &Path) -> Result<GateResult>;\n\n    /// Gate type name for telemetry and configuration (e.g., \"command\", \"custom\").\n    fn gate_type(&self) -> &str;\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Gate Registry\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Registry for pluggable validation gates.\n///\n/// Gates are registered by type name. The registry is thread-safe and supports\n/// dynamic registration of custom gate types.\npub struct GateRegistry {\n    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]\n    gates: RwLock<HashMap<String, Arc<dyn Fn(&GateConfig) -> Result<Arc<dyn Gate>> + Send + Sync>>>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for GateRegistry {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl GateRegistry {\n    /// Create a new registry with built-in gate types registered.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let registry = GateRegistry {\n            gates: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),\n        };\n        // Register built-in gate types\n        registry.register_builtin_gates();\n        registry\n    }\n\n    /// Register a built-in gate type constructor.\n    fn register_builtin_gates(&self) {\n        self.register(\"command\", |config| match config {\n            GateConfig::Command {\n                commands,\n                stderr_cap_bytes,\n            } => Ok(Arc::new(CommandGate::with_stderr_cap(\n                commands.clone(),\n                stderr_cap_bytes.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_STDERR_CAP_BYTES),\n            ))),\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Register a custom gate type constructor.\n    ///\n    /// The constructor function takes a `GateConfig` and returns a boxed `Gate`.\n    /// Custom gates should parse their config from the `GateConfig` enum.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```ignore\n    /// registry.register(\"my_gate\", |config| {\n    ///     // Parse config and create custom gate\n    ///     Ok(Arc::new(MyCustomGate::new(config)?))\n    /// });\n    /// ```\n    pub fn register<F>(&self, gate_type: impl Into<String>, constructor: F)\n    where\n        F: Fn(&GateConfig) -> Result<Arc<dyn Gate>> + Send + Sync + 'static,\n    {\n        let gate_type = gate_type.into();\n        let mut guards = self.gates.write().unwrap();\n        guards.insert(gate_type, Arc::new(constructor));\n    }\n\n    /// Create a gate instance from its configuration.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the gate type is not registered or construction fails.\n    pub fn create_gate(&self, config: &GateConfig) -> Result<Arc<dyn Gate>> {\n        let gate_type = match config {\n            GateConfig::Command { .. } => \"command\",\n        };\n\n        let guards = self.gates.read().unwrap();\n        let constructor = guards\n            .get(gate_type)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"unknown gate type '{}': not registered\", gate_type))?;\n\n        constructor(config)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the global gate registry instance.\n    pub fn global() -> &'static GateRegistry {\n        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n        static REGISTRY: OnceLock<GateRegistry> = OnceLock::new();\n        REGISTRY.get_or_init(GateRegistry::new)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Built-in Gate Types\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Default stderr capture cap (bytes) — preserves the previous hardcoded value.\nconst DEFAULT_STDERR_CAP_BYTES: usize = 4096;\n\n/// Runs configured shell commands as validation gates.\npub struct CommandGate {\n    commands: Vec<String>,\n    /// Maximum bytes of stderr captured on failure. Configurable via\n    /// `validation.stderr_cap_bytes` — see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#9.\n    stderr_cap_bytes: usize,\n}\n\nimpl CommandGate {\n    /// Create a new command gate with the default stderr cap (4096 bytes).\n    pub fn new(commands: Vec<String>) -> Self {\n        Self::with_stderr_cap(commands, DEFAULT_STDERR_CAP_BYTES)\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new command gate with an explicit stderr capture cap.\n    pub fn with_stderr_cap(commands: Vec<String>, stderr_cap_bytes: usize) -> Self {\n        CommandGate {\n            commands,\n            stderr_cap_bytes,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl Gate for CommandGate {\n    async fn validate(&self, bead: &crate::types::Bead, workspace: &Path) -> Result<GateResult> {\n        // Run commands sequentially; stop at first failure.\n        for cmd in &self.commands {\n            tracing::info!(\n                command = %cmd,\n                workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                \"running command gate\"\n            );\n\n            match self.run_command(cmd, bead, workspace).await {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    tracing::info!(command = %cmd, \"command gate passed\");\n                }\n                Err(failure) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        command = %cmd,\n                        exit_code = ?failure.exit_code,\n                        \"command gate failed\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(GateResult::Fail(format!(\n                        \"command '{}' failed: {}\",\n                        cmd,\n                        failure.output.trim()\n                    )));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(GateResult::Pass)\n    }\n\n    fn gate_type(&self) -> &str {\n        \"command\"\n    }\n}\n\nimpl CommandGate {\n    /// Run a single command. Returns `Ok(())` on exit 0, `Err(GateFailure)` otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// The command's environment carries `NEEDLE_BEAD_ID` and `NEEDLE_WORKSPACE`\n    /// so a gate can identify the bead it is judging without racily guessing it\n    /// from external state (e.g. `br list --json` assignee) — see GitHub issue\n    /// jedarden/NEEDLE#7.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `tokio::process::Command` (not `std::process::Command`) with\n    /// `kill_on_drop(true)`: this makes the command a genuine `.await` yield\n    /// point, so `OutcomeHandler::handle_with_cancellation`'s\n    /// `tokio::time::timeout` can actually abandon and kill a gate command\n    /// that outruns `validation.outcome_timeout_seconds`, instead of only\n    /// observing after the fact that it ran too long (see bf-3saat — a\n    /// blocking `std::process::Command` call has no yield point, so a\n    /// wrapping timeout can never preempt it mid-command).\n    async fn run_command(\n        &self,\n        cmd: &str,\n        bead: &crate::types::Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> std::result::Result<(), GateFailure> {\n        let result = tokio::process::Command::new(\"sh\")\n            .arg(\"-c\")\n            .arg(cmd)\n            .current_dir(workspace)\n            .env(\"NEEDLE_BEAD_ID\", bead.id.to_string())\n            .env(\"NEEDLE_WORKSPACE\", workspace.display().to_string())\n            .kill_on_drop(true)\n            .output()\n            .await;\n\n        match result {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if output.status.success() {\n                    Ok(())\n                } else {\n                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n                    let truncated = truncate_output(&stderr, self.stderr_cap_bytes);\n                    Err(GateFailure {\n                        command: cmd.to_string(),\n                        exit_code: output.status.code(),\n                        output: truncated,\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => Err(GateFailure {\n                command: cmd.to_string(),\n                exit_code: None,\n                output: format!(\"failed to execute command: {}\", e),\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Truncate output to at most `max_bytes`, adding an ellipsis if truncated.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str, max_bytes: usize) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= max_bytes {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..max_bytes];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ValidationGate (Main Entry Point)\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runs configured verification gates in a workspace directory.\n///\n/// This is the main entry point for validation. It uses the pluggable gate\n/// system to run all configured gates and returns an aggregated report.\npub struct ValidationGate {\n    gates: Vec<(String, Arc<dyn Gate>)>,\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl ValidationGate {\n    /// Create a new validation gate from gate configurations.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if `gate_configs` is empty (no verification configured).\n    pub fn new(gate_configs: Vec<(String, GateConfig)>, workspace: PathBuf) -> Option<Self> {\n        if gate_configs.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        let registry = GateRegistry::global();\n        let mut gates = Vec::new();\n\n        for (name, config) in gate_configs {\n            match registry.create_gate(&config) {\n                Ok(gate) => gates.push((name, gate)),\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        gate_name = %name,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to create gate — skipping\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if gates.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        Some(ValidationGate { gates, workspace })\n    }\n\n    /// Create from legacy command list (backwards compatibility).\n    ///\n    /// This method maintains the existing API for code that uses `Vec<String>`\n    /// for verification commands. Uses the default stderr cap (4096 bytes);\n    /// use [`Self::from_commands_with_stderr_cap`] to configure it.\n    pub fn from_commands(commands: Vec<String>, workspace: PathBuf) -> Option<Self> {\n        Self::from_commands_with_stderr_cap(commands, workspace, DEFAULT_STDERR_CAP_BYTES)\n    }\n\n    /// Create from legacy command list with an explicit stderr capture cap.\n    ///\n    /// See GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#9 — used by\n    /// `OutcomeHandler::handle_success` to apply `validation.stderr_cap_bytes`\n    /// to the legacy `verification:` config format.\n    pub fn from_commands_with_stderr_cap(\n        commands: Vec<String>,\n        workspace: PathBuf,\n        stderr_cap_bytes: usize,\n    ) -> Option<Self> {\n        if commands.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let gate = Arc::new(CommandGate::with_stderr_cap(commands, stderr_cap_bytes));\n        Some(ValidationGate {\n            gates: vec![(\"command_gate\".to_string(), gate as Arc<dyn Gate>)],\n            workspace,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Run all gates sequentially. Stops at the first failure.\n    pub async fn run(&self, bead: &crate::types::Bead) -> Result<GateReport> {\n        let mut results = HashMap::new();\n\n        for (name, gate) in &self.gates {\n            let result = gate.validate(bead, &self.workspace).await?;\n            results.insert(name.clone(), result);\n\n            // Stop on first failure.\n            if !results.values().all(|r| r.passed()) {\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(GateReport::new(results))\n    }\n\n    /// Workspace directory where gates run.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// observe it after the fact.\n        // Simulate that here directly: race the gate's future against a short\n        // timeout and confirm (a) the timeout wins and (b) the child process\n        // is Shipped-work verification: did a bead's closure correspond to real,\n//! durable output?\n//!\n//! Gated by `worker.enforce_shipped_work` (default `true`). Runs only when an\n//! agent has already closed the bead (see `outcome::handle_success`). Passes\n//! if either:\n//! - a commit was made since dispatch started (per the `validation::predispatch`\n//!   snapshot) that touches at least one file outside `notes/`/`.beads/`, and\n//!   that commit has been pushed to the upstream remote; or\n//! - the bead's own `notes` field changed during this dispatch — i.e. the agent\n//!   recorded a bead note explaining why no code change was needed.\n//!\n//! With no snapshot the gate has no baseline and **fails open** — it cannot tell\n//! a commit made during the dispatch from one that predates it, and releasing on\n//! \"don't know\" would recreate the retry loop it exists to stop.\n//!\n//! Deliberately does NOT accept a commit touching only `notes/`/`.beads/` as\n//! sufficient on its own: a prior incident (see docs/notes on ARMOR's\n//! commit-storm) showed a worker stuck retrying an uncompletable bead will\n//! happily satisfy a bare \"must have a commit\" rule by committing a trivial\n//! \"still blocked\" doc file every cycle, each one triggering paired CI\n//! version-bump commits. Recording that kind of status belongs on the bead\n//! through the workspace's configured backend, not in git history.\n//!\n//! # Why not `updated_at`\n//!\n//! The original fallback compared `post.updated_at > pre.updated_at`. That is\n//! unsound: `bf close` *is* an update, so the timestamp always advances on the\n//! exact path the gate exists to judge — an agent that closed a bead having\n//! shipped nothing. Combined with a missing snapshot writer, this made the gate\n//! inert from the day it shipped (2026-07-30) until this change: no closure was\n//! ever rejected, and no bead ever received the `verification-failed` label.\n//! Fail\n    // OPEN. Releasing on \"don't know\" would re-release every closure whenever\n    // snapshot recording failed — the same unbounded retry loop this gate\n    // exists to stop, just triggered from the other side.\n    let Some(snapshot) = snapshot else {\n        tracing::debug!(\n            workspace = %workspace.display(),\n            \"no pre-dispatch snapshot — shipped-work gate passing without a verdict\"\n        );\n        return Ok(GateResult::Pass);\n    };\n\n    if let Some(result) = check_commit(workspace, Some(snapshot)).await? {\n        return Ok(result);\n    }\n\n    // Fallback: the agent recorded an explanation on the bead itself.\n    match snapshot.notes_hash.as_deref() {\n        Some(pre_hash) => {\n            if hash_notes(post_notes) != pre_hash {\n                return Ok(GateResult::Pass);\n            }\n        }\n        None => {\n            // Notes were unreadable at dispatch, so there is nothing to diff\n            // against. Before each dispatch the worker records the workspace's git HEAD and a hash\n//! of the bead's `notes` field. `validation::shipped_work` compares against this\n//! snapshot to decide whether a closure corresponded to real output.\n//!\n//! **Snapshots live under `~/.needle/state/predispatch/`, never in the\n//! workspace.** The gate originally specified a `.needle-predispatch-sha` file\n//! inside the repo.
